parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The virus that causes the infectious disease influenza has two antigens, H and N.
Antibodies are produced in response to an infection by this virus. The antibodies are
specific for either antigen H or for antigen N.
Describe how the structure of an antibody molecule allows it to be specific for one
antigen, such as H or N.

parts.text: Cholera is a disease caused by a bacterial pathogen.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Name the pathogen that causes cholera.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Describe how the pathogen that causes cholera is transmitted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Viruses that infect bacteria are called bacteriophages. Some bacteriophages that infect the
cholera pathogen cause lysis of the bacterium.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest what happens to the structure of a bacterial cell to cause lysis.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Some scientists believe that bacteriophages could be used to treat people who are
infected with cholera.
Suggest the properties of the bacteriophages that would make this possible.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Antibiotics can be used to treat people with cholera.
State why antibiotics are not effective against measles.
